answers.answer: In the 3-player case, the tied leaders gain no coin; the uniquely last player pays 1 coin. In a 2-player unequal Census, the unique leader still gains 1 coin, but the last player never pays.
answers.evidence: Census: a tied lead gives no coin; a tied last place pays nothing. In a 2-player game the last player never pays, but a unique leader still gains 1 coin.

answers.answer: You do not have to draw six: draw any number up to the allowance, limited by your two free Market spaces. You cannot draw more than two. Undrawn Market Followers remain there between rounds and occupy capacity.
answers.evidence: Draw any number up to the allowance ... limited by free Market spaces. Unused Market Followers remain between rounds and occupy capacity.

answers.answer: You may fill an action gradually over multiple rounds. You cannot execute it until all its required spaces are occupied (except Town Hall, which needs only one of its two spaces); a fully activated action may be saved for a later round. When executed, its Followers return to your bag; Technology remains on its spaces.
answers.evidence: You may ... fill an action gradually over multiple rounds. An action is activated only when all required spaces are occupied ... An activation can be saved for a later round.

answers.answer: Starting with the Start Player and moving clockwise repeatedly, players take one activated action or pass per turn. Passing ends your participation for that Action Phase, so you cannot act again that round. Your unused activation retains its Followers on the board for future rounds.
answers.evidence: Taking one activated action or passing per turn ... Passing ends your participation ... Unused activations ... keep their Followers on the board for future rounds.

answers.answer: Farm House recruits a Farmer into your bag, advances your Farmers Track one space, and gives the good depicted at the new track space.
answers.evidence: Farm House: ... Put a new Farmer in your bag; advance Farmers Track one space and take its depicted good.

answers.answer: Village can recruit a Boatman, Craftsman, or Trader, putting the chosen neutral Follower in your bag and advancing that profession's track one space. Boatman gives the depicted coins, except at the last space where the first player there gets a Citizen instead. Craftsman gives a Technology tile, usable only after you pass. Trader gives a Place Tile: the first track advance allows category I only, while later advances allow category I or II.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment: Put the chosen neutral Follower into your bag and advance its profession's track one space.

answers.answer: No. A newly acquired Craftsman Technology is usable only after you pass, so it cannot help another action that Action Phase after that pass. The first Technology must replace a Farmer. Each Technology permanently fills one required Action Space and stays there; later ones may replace any profession except Monk. You may not place more than one Technology at one Place or any Technology at a Place requiring only one Follower.
answers.evidence: A Craftsman-acquired tile is used only after passing. Your first placed Technology must replace a Farmer; later ones may replace any profession except Monk.

answers.answer: No. The first Trader-track advance permits category I only; every later advance allows category I or II. Players may inspect both stacks at any time.
answers.evidence: Your first Traders Track advance permits category I only; every later advance allows I or II. Players may inspect these stacks at any time.

answers.answer: University recruits a Scholar into your bag, advances the Scholars Track one space, and grants its depicted Development Points. Castle recruits a Knight into your bag and advances the Knights Track one space. Monastery recruits a Monk into your bag with no extra track reward. Recruiting the fourth Knight does not increase the draw allowance above 7 at that step; the first player there may receive the Citizen. Once a character track is at its last space, you cannot take its corresponding action again.
answers.evidence: University ... put a new Scholar in your bag; advance Scholars Track ... Castle ... put a new Knight in your bag; advance Knights Track ... Monastery ... put a new Monk in your bag; no extra track reward.

answers.answer: A Monk may replace a Knight for an ordinary action. A Knight or Technology cannot replace a required Monk. A Monk also cannot replace a profession on Beneficial Deeds, which require the exact professions depicted.
answers.evidence: On ordinary actions, a Monk can replace any other profession. The reverse is forbidden ... Substitutions, including Monks ... cannot replace the exact professions depicted on Deeds.

answers.answer: One Ship action moves the Merchant one adjacent town along one Waterway; one Wagon action moves it one adjacent town along one Road. You may take at most one good from that connection, choosing one if two lie there. An empty connection is legal and yields no good.
answers.evidence: One Ship/Wagon action traverses just one connection. You may take one good from that connection ... Empty Roads/Waterways are legal and yield no good.

answers.answer: Guildhall builds one Trading Station in the Merchant's current town. Your Merchant must be there. A town with any player's station cannot receive another, except Orléans, where each player may build one station.
answers.evidence: Build one Trading Station in your Merchant's current town ... A town with any player's Trading Station cannot receive another. Orléans is the exception.

answers.answer: Scriptorium grants 1 Development Point, moving one space on the Development Track. When movement lands on or passes a coin space, collect its depicted coins; the first player onto or past a Citizen space collects that Citizen. Reaching or passing a Development Status space immediately changes your Status to its shown value.
answers.evidence: Scriptorium: Gain 1 Development Point: move one space ... On moving onto or past a coin space, collect ... first player ... Citizen ... Status immediately becomes its shown value.

answers.answer: Town Hall works with one or two eligible Followers in one action; starting marked Followers cannot be used. Send one or both to free Deed spaces matching their exact professions, including spaces on different Deeds. Each placement earns the depicted 1, 2, or 3 coins; Canalization gives a choice of 1 coin or 1 Development Point. The player who fills a Deed's last unoccupied space takes its Citizen. Sent Followers stay there for the rest of the game.
answers.evidence: In one Town Hall action, send one or both to any free Deed spaces matching their exact professions ... for Canalization choose 1 coin or 1 Development Point. Whoever fills a Deed's last unoccupied space takes its Citizen.

answers.answer: Pilgrimage forbids Monk recruitment during that round's Action Phase; it applies before the Event Phase, during Phase 5. Other events resolve in Phase 6. The game opens with Pilgrimage because that tile is placed on top of the Hour Glass stack.
answers.evidence: Pilgrimage instead prohibits Monk recruitment during Phase 5 ... Most events wait until Phase 6 ... round 1 always has Pilgrimage.

answers.answer: Wine qualifies as food; wool does not. Paid food goes to the Goods Market. If you cannot pay food, you owe 5 coins; with fewer than five coins, you pay what you have and undergo torture for the shortfall.
answers.evidence: Harvest: Pay one grain, cheese, or wine to the Goods Market. If you cannot pay food, pay 5 coins instead. If unable to pay those coins, undergo torture for the shortfall. Wool and brocade are not food.

answers.answer: The neutral Scholar is returned to its game-board supply and becomes recruitable again; its track marker does not move back. The colored starting Trader is kept, so no Follower is lost and no replacement draw is required. Starting Followers cannot be lost to Plague.
answers.evidence: A neutral Follower returns to its game-board supply ... do not move its track marker back. If it is one of your marked starting Followers, keep it and lose no Follower this round; do not redraw.

answers.answer: Pay the one available coin, then replace each of the two missing coins with an eligible item, in any mix: a built or unbuilt Trading Station; one random eligible neutral Follower from your bag; one Development Point; or one Goods, Place, or Technology tile. For Followers, return and redraw marked starting Followers until drawing a neutral one. A Development Point moves one space left but cannot move onto or past a coin space. Surrendered items are removed from the game. Marked starting Followers cannot be sacrificed.
answers.evidence: Replace each missing coin with one item from any mix ... return and redraw marked starting Followers until drawing an eligible neutral one ... Development Point ... never onto or past a coin space. Items surrendered ... removed from the game.

answers.answer: You cannot play an action that provides an unavailable Character, Technology, or Goods tile, even if another part would still give a reward. The summary says returned goods or Followers can make corresponding actions available again, but does not explicitly state a general rule for resuming an unavailable action when stock returns. If the common coin supply is temporarily empty, players cannot receive coins at that moment.
answers.evidence: You cannot play an action that provides an unavailable tile ... Harvest and Plague may return goods/Followers to supply; the corresponding actions become available again. If the common supply has insufficient coins, players cannot receive coins at that moment.

answers.answer: A tie for most built Trading Stations means nobody takes the bonus Citizen. Goods score grain 1, cheese 2, wine 3, wool 4, and brocade 5 points each. Stations and collected Citizens score (built stations + Citizens) multiplied by final Development Status. For tied final scores, the player furthest ahead on the Development Track wins; if still tied, they share victory.
answers.evidence: A tie gives nobody that Citizen. Goods ... 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 each. Highest total wins. Ties go to the player furthest ahead on the Development Track; if still tied, share victory.
